---
title: "Wind Statistics - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

The data have been modified to contain some missing values, identified by NaN.
Using dplyr and tidyr should make this exercise
easier, in particular for the bonus question.

You should be able to perform all of these operations without using
a for loop or other looping construct.

1. The data in 'wind.data' has the following format:

```
Yr Mo Dy   RPT   VAL   ROS   KIL   SHA   BIR   DUB   CLA   MUL   CLO   BEL   MAL
61  1  1 15.04 14.96 13.17  9.29   NaN  9.87 13.67 10.25 10.83 12.58 18.50 15.04
61  1  2 14.71   NaN 10.83  6.50 12.62  7.67 11.50 10.04  9.79  9.67 17.54 13.83
61  1  3 18.50 16.88 12.33 10.13 11.17  6.17 11.25   NaN  8.50  7.67 12.75 12.71
```

The first three columns are year, month and day. The
remaining 12 columns are average windspeeds in knots at 12
locations in Ireland on that day.

More information about the dataset go [here](wind.desc).

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://github.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/blob/master/06_Stats/Wind_Stats/wind.data)

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called data and replace the first 3 columns by a proper date column.

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_table("wind.data", na = "NaN")
data_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/06_Stats/Wind_Stats/wind.data"

# read_table() reads columns separated by any amount of white space
data <- read_table(data_url, na = c("NaN", "NA"))

# ymd() parses "61 1 1" as year-month-day
data <- data |>
  mutate(Yr_Mo_Dy = ymd(paste(Yr, Mo, Dy)), .before = 1) |>
  select(-Yr, -Mo, -Dy)

head(data)
```

### Step 4. Year 2061? Do we really have data from this year? Create a function to fix it and apply it.

```{r}
# The problem is that two-digit years below 69 are read as 20xx...

# function that subtracts 100 years when the year is in the future
fix_century <- function(x) {
  if_else(year(x) > 1989, x - years(100), x)
}

# apply the function fix_century on the column and replace the values
data <- data |> mutate(Yr_Mo_Dy = fix_century(Yr_Mo_Dy))

head(data)
```

### Step 5. Set the right dates as the index. Pay attention at the data type, it should be Date.

```{r}
# tibbles have no index: Yr_Mo_Dy stays as the first column, sorted by date
class(data$Yr_Mo_Dy)

data <- data |> arrange(Yr_Mo_Dy)
head(data)
```

### Step 6. Compute how many values are missing for each location over the entire record.

#### They should be ignored in all calculations below.

```{r}
data |> summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) sum(is.na(x))))
```

### Step 7. Compute how many non-missing values there are in total.

```{r}
# for each location
data |> summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) sum(!is.na(x))))

# in total
sum(!is.na(select(data, -Yr_Mo_Dy)))
```

### Step 8. Calculate the mean windspeeds of the windspeeds over all the locations and all the times.

#### A single number for the entire dataset.

```{r}
data |>
  select(-Yr_Mo_Dy) |>
  as.matrix() |>
  mean(na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Step 9. Create a DataFrame called loc_stats and calculate the min, max and mean windspeeds and standard deviations of the windspeeds at each location over all the days

#### A different set of numbers for each location.

```{r}
# long format: one row per day and location
data_long <- data |>
  pivot_longer(-Yr_Mo_Dy, names_to = "location", values_to = "speed") |>
  mutate(location = factor(location, levels = names(data)[-1])) # keep the original order

loc_stats <- data_long |>
  group_by(location) |>
  summarise(min = min(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            std = sd(speed, na.rm = TRUE))

loc_stats
```

### Step 10. Create a DataFrame called day_stats and calculate the min, max and mean windspeed and standard deviations of the windspeeds across all the locations at each day.

#### A different set of numbers for each day.

```{r}
day_stats <- data_long |>
  group_by(Yr_Mo_Dy) |>
  summarise(min = min(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            std = sd(speed, na.rm = TRUE))

head(day_stats)
```

### Step 11. Find the average windspeed in January for each location.

#### Treat January 1961 and January 1962 both as January.

```{r}
data |>
  filter(month(Yr_Mo_Dy) == 1) |>
  summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### Step 12. Downsample the record to a yearly frequency for each location.

```{r}
data |>
  group_by(year = year(Yr_Mo_Dy)) |>
  summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### Step 13. Downsample the record to a monthly frequency for each location.

```{r}
data |>
  group_by(month = floor_date(Yr_Mo_Dy, "month")) |>
  summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### Step 14. Downsample the record to a weekly frequency for each location.

```{r}
# weeks starting on Monday (week_start = 1)
data |>
  group_by(week = floor_date(Yr_Mo_Dy, "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  summarise(across(-Yr_Mo_Dy, \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

### Step 15. Calculate the min, max and mean windspeeds and standard deviations of the windspeeds across all locations for each week (assume that the first week starts on January 2 1961) for the first 52 weeks.

```{r}
weekly <- data_long |>
  filter(Yr_Mo_Dy >= ymd("1961-01-02")) |>
  mutate(week = floor_date(Yr_Mo_Dy, "week", week_start = 1)) |>
  # keep only the first 52 weeks
  filter(week < ymd("1961-01-02") + weeks(52)) |>
  group_by(week, location) |>
  summarise(min = min(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            std = sd(speed, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

head(weekly, 10)

# one row per week, with the statistics of each location in columns
weekly |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = location, values_from = c(min, max, mean, std),
              names_glue = "{location}_{.value}", names_vary = "slowest") |>
  head(10)
```
